topIssues.title: RPC Performance: Prevent eth_getLogs memory exhaustion (Upstream Geth fixes available)
topIssues.author: locoholy
topIssues.body:
### Description
Currently, `op-geth` is vulnerable to the same `eth_getLogs` memory exhaustion loop that hits upstream `go-ethereum` when serving wide block ranges. Unbounded state scans can lead to severe memory spikes (OOMs) on RPC nodes, especially under heavy indexer load.

My team recently authored and merged the definitive fixes for this into upstream `go-ethereum`. We implemented bounded state scans and strict memory queue limits that prevent the node from crashing while keeping latency stable.

**Here are our upstream PRs implementing these limits:**
* eth: add admin_capabilities RPC method: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/33886
* eth/filters: cap polling filter queues to prevent unbounded memory growth: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/33885
* ethclient: omit empty address/topics in RPC filter requests: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/33884
* eth/filters: add optional getLogs limit support: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/33881

### Proposal
Since `op-geth` is fundamentally Geth under the hood, we can help the execution client maintainers cleanly port these optimizations down to your architecture. This will dramatically save your RPC infrastructure providers from hardware overhead and network stalls.

If the core engineering team is interested in syncing on this, we are happy to put together a technical proposal (or RetroPGF submission) to implement these safeguards natively for Optimism. Let us know who to coordinate with!

topIssues.title: miner: makeEnv historical state fallback is unreachable on full nodes using path-based state scheme
topIssues.author: sentientpanic
topIssues.body:
Hi Folks - I'm new to OP Stack, so apologies in advance if I am misunderstanding anything. Thanks in advance for the help.

#### System information

Geth version: op-geth (path-based state scheme, --state.scheme=path)
CL client & version: op-node
OS & Version: Linux
Commit hash: optimism branch (HEAD)

#### Expected behaviour

When op-node's derivation pipeline lags significantly behind op-geth's chain tip, [`makeEnv()` in the block builder](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/optimism/miner/worker.go#L376-L394) should be able to build blocks from any parent for which the node maintains state. 
For path-based nodes, if the desired parent is beyond the 128-block in-memory diff layer limit, the node should fall back to reconstructing parent state from the on-disk state history (for path-based nodes this would be controlled by `--history.state`, which defaults to 90,000 blocks). 

#### Actual behaviour

When the parent block is more than ~128 blocks behind op-geth's chain tip, [`StateAt()` fails](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/optimism/miner/worker.go#L379) with missing trie node because the state root is no longer in the in-memory diff layers. 
Importantly, the [`StateAtBlock()` fallback](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/optimism/miner/worker.go#L383-L394), which would access the on-disk state history, is never reached. 
This is as a result of two issues:
1. `makeEnv()` returns early on `StateAt` failure before the fallback is reached.
2. Since the miner's backend is `*Ethereum`, the `BackendWithHistoricalState` type assertion always fails, because it doesn't export the expected `StateAtBlock()`

The result is that the missing trie node error propagates as `InvalidPayloadAttributes` back to op-node, which results in a critical error.

#### Steps to reproduce the behaviour

1. Run op-geth with `--state.scheme=path` (default --history.state=90000)
2. Run op-node in a configuration where the unsafe head can advance ahead of the safe head (e.g., EL sync mode, or any scenario where the derivation pipeline falls behind - slow L1 RPC, pipeline reset, etc.)
3. Allow a gap of >128 blocks to form between the derivation pipeline position and op-geth's chain tip
4. The derivation pipeline attempts to build a block whose parent is >128 blocks behind the tip
5. op-node crashes with a critical error


#### Backtrace


topPRs.title: fix: Use sync txpool.Add in TestInteropTxRejectedWithFailsafe
topPRs.author: piersy
topPRs.body:
Not using sync can lead to race conditions and cause the test to fail randomly.

Very small PR, with a very small fix.
